name: Introduction to forces and types of forces

questions.q: What is the scientific definition of a force in physics?
a: A push or a pull acting upon an object
The amount of matter inside a body
The speed at which an object travels
The total energy stored in an object

questions.q: What is the standard SI unit used to measure force?
Which instrument is standardly used to measure the size of a force in a school laboratory?
Which of the following effects can a force produce on an object?
a: Change its shape, speed, or direction of motion

questions.q: What type of force is friction?
a: A contact force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact
A force that creates infinite energy

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a non-contact (action-at-a-distance) force?
What term describes the force exerted by a stretched or compressed spring or elastic band?
When a skydiver falls through the air, what upward force acts against gravity due to collision with air particles?
What do we call forces that are equal in size but opposite in direction acting on an object, resulting in zero net force?
If two opposing forces acting on a box are unbalanced (for example, a larger push to the right and a smaller friction to the left), what will happen to the box?
a: It will accelerate in the direction of the larger force
It will float into the air

questions.q: What is the upward force exerted by a surface (such as a table) to support an object resting on it called?
Which of these forces acts when two electrical charges interact or when static electricity causes hair to stand up?
Why does a rolling football eventually slow down and stop on a flat grass pitch?
a: Friction from the grass and air resistance create an unbalanced opposing force
The ball runs out of matter

questions.q: Which scientific diagram tool is used to show the direction and relative size of all forces acting on an object?
What force allows a person to walk forward without slipping on a dry pavement?
a: Friction between the shoes and the ground

questions.q: What happens when you apply a pair of balanced forces to a stationary book resting on a table?
a: The book changes shape into a sphere
The book flies off the table

questions.q: Which of the following is a contact force experienced when pulling a heavy object using a string or cable?
If a parachute is opened by a skydiver, why does air resistance increase significantly?
a: The large surface area of the parachute collides with many more air particles

questions.q: What is the term for the overall single force that replaces multiple forces acting on an object?
Which force pulls objects toward the center of the Earth without any physical contact?
Why do engineers use lubricants like oil or grease on moving metal parts of a machine?
a: To reduce unwanted friction and wear and tear between surfaces
To increase the weight of the machine

questions.q: Which of the following pairs contains only contact forces?
What force causes iron nails to be pulled toward a bar magnet?
If an object is moving at a steady constant speed in a straight line, what can be deduced about the forces acting on it?
a: There are no forces acting on it at all
The forward force is much greater than friction
Friction is greater than the pushing force
The forces acting on it are balanced (resultant force is zero)

questions.q: What name is given to the resistance experienced by an object moving through water or any other fluid?
Which of the following everyday activities relies heavily on increasing friction rather than reducing it?
a: Applying rubber treads on car tyres for rainy roads
Putting oil on bicycle chain gears
Sliding down a polished metal slide

questions.q: What scientific instrument uses a calibrated spring to measure the magnitude of applied forces?
When a gymnast hangs stationary from a high bar, what two main forces are acting on the gymnast in balance?
a: Downward pull of gravity and upward tension in the arms/bar

questions.q: What happens to the extension of a spring if you double the stretching force applied to it (within its elastic limit)?
Which of these forces is responsible for keeping planets in orbit around the Sun?
What is the main reason streamlining (such as a teardrop shape) is used on cars, trains, and airplanes?
a: To reduce air resistance (drag) at high speeds

questions.q: If a box has a 50 N force pulling it to the right and a 30 N friction force pushing back to the left, what is the magnitude and direction of the resultant force?
What is the term for a push or pull that can change the motion or shape of an object?
Which physical property determines how much a spring stretches when a specific force is applied?
What kind of force occurs when rubbing a plastic ruler with a dry cloth causes small paper scraps to stick to it?
Which of the following best describes the effect of balanced forces on a moving bicycle?
a: The bicycle will speed up rapidly
The bicycle will come to an immediate halt
The bicycle will continue moving at a constant speed in a straight line

questions.q: What type of force opposes the relative motion of solid surfaces sliding past each other?
Why do wet ceramic kitchen floors present a slipping hazard compared to dry carpets?
a: Water acts as a lubricant, drastically reducing friction between shoes and the floor

questions.q: If a spring stretches by 2 cm under a 4 N load, how much will it stretch under an 8 N load (assuming it stays within its elastic limit)?
What is the primary factor that determines whether a force is classified as a contact force or a non-contact force?
a: Whether the objects are made of metal
Whether the force is measured in Newtons
Whether the objects need to physically touch each other to exert the force
